summary: Amends the Clean Air Act to exclude from the definition of solid waste incineration unit any facility that converts plastic or post-use polymers via pyrolysis, gasification, or similar processes into outputs that are at least 50 percent products by mass, and creates a petition process for other such facilities.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations. It is solely a regulatory amendment to the Clean Air Act.
No tax provisions, credits, deductions, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not address immigration, border policy, or related enforcement.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No military, defense, or national security spending or policy elements.

The bill directly amends Section 129 of the Clean Air Act to exclude certain plastic/post-use polymer conversion facilities (using pyrolysis, gasification, etc.) from the definition of 'solid waste incineration unit' when at least 50% of outputs are usable products. This reclassification removes these facilities from associated Clean Air Act emission standards and permitting requirements that would otherwise apply to incinerators. The explicit goal is regulatory relief for chemical recycling technologies, which constitutes a clear limitation on environmental regulation.
